description.en: Understand how a router remembers just “a network” instead of billions of hosts: the prefix of an address, how address blocks are cut and merged, longest prefix matching, and what every field in an IPv4 datagram header is for.
description.zh: 看懂路由器怎样只记「一个网络」而不是几十亿台主机：地址的前缀、地址块怎么切怎么合、最长前缀匹配，以及 IPv4 数据报头里每个字段是做什么的。

name.zh: IPv4 地址与前缀 (IPv4 addresses, prefixes)
子网掩码与路由表 (subnet mask, routing tables)
无类别域间路由与路由聚合 (CIDR, aggregation)
最长前缀匹配 (longest matching prefix)
IPv4 数据报格式 (IPv4 datagram structure)
IP 地址、前缀与子网划分 (IP prefix, subnetting)

description.en: Thinking an IP address is just a host's number, unrelated to location. In fact it has a network part, so you can tell at a glance which network it is in, and that is what lets routers remember only networks.
description.zh: 以为 IP 地址只是主机的编号，和位置无关。其实它有网络部分，一看就知道在哪个网络，路由器才能只记网络。

description.en: Thinking an address block can start at any address. In fact a /L block must start at a multiple of the block size.
description.zh: 以为地址块可以从任意地址开始。其实 /L 的块，起点必须是块大小的整数倍。

description.en: Thinking only one row of the routing table matches, or taking the first matching row. In fact several rows may match, and the one with the longest prefix must be taken.
description.zh: 以为路由表里匹配的行只有一行，或者取第一个匹配的行。其实可能多行匹配，要取前缀最长的。

description.en: Thinking any prefixes can be merged. In fact they must be contiguous, aligned, and completely covered by one shorter prefix, otherwise the merged route will attract other people's packets.
description.zh: 以为任意几个前缀都能合并。其实要连续、对齐，并被一个更短的前缀完整覆盖，否则会吸来别人的包。

description.en: Thinking IP's header checksum also protects the payload. In fact it covers only the header; the transport layer checks the payload itself.
description.zh: 以为 IP 的头部校验和也保护载荷。其实它只管头部，载荷由传输层自己校验。

description.en: Taking MF for the end bit of the previous lesson. In fact it is the opposite: MF = 1 means more follow, and the last fragment has MF = 0.
description.zh: 把 MF 当成上一课的结束位。其实正相反：MF = 1 表示后面还有，最后一片 MF = 0。

description.en: Taking the fragment offset as a number of bytes. In fact it is in units of 8 bytes.
description.zh: 把片偏移当成字节数。其实它以 8 字节为单位。

title.en: One row or two hundred and fifty-six
title.zh: 一行还是两百五十六行

prompt.en: An organisation owns the 256 addresses 128.18.3.0 to 128.18.3.255. A distant router must send all packets for these 256 addresses in the same direction. What is the fewest rows its routing table needs to represent them?
prompt.zh: 一个单位拥有 128.18.3.0 到 128.18.3.255 共 256 个地址。远处的路由器要把发往这 256 个地址的包都送同一个方向。它的路由表里，最少需要几行才能表示？

feedback.en: With billions of addresses worldwide, the table would be far too big to store. We have to rely on the hierarchy of the address itself.
feedback.zh: 这样全球几十亿个地址，表就大得存不下。要靠地址本身的层次。

label.en: 1 row: these 256 addresses have the same beginning, so one row can stand for them.
label.zh: 1 行：这 256 个地址有同一个开头，一行就能代表。

label.en: 2 rows: one for the first 128, one for the last 128.
label.zh: 2 行：一行管前 128 个，一行管后 128 个。

feedback.en: No need to split: their first 24 bits are exactly the same, so one row can say it all.
feedback.zh: 没有必要拆开：它们的前 24 位完全相同，一行就能说完。

label.en: 8 rows: one for each binary bit.
label.zh: 8 行：每一位二进制对应一行。

feedback.en: A row in the table corresponds to a whole address block, not to a single bit.
feedback.zh: 表里的一行对应的是一整个地址块，不是某一位。

explain.en: The first 24 bits of these 256 addresses are all the same; only the last 8 bits vary. The router just has to say “anything whose first 24 bits are 128.18.3 goes this way”, and one row is enough. Addresses have a hierarchy, so routers can remember only “a network”. This lesson is about exactly this method.
explain.zh: 这 256 个地址前 24 位都相同，只有最后 8 位在变。路由器只要说「前 24 位是 128.18.3 的，都往这边」，一行就够。地址有层次，路由器才能只记「一个网络」。这一课讲的就是这个办法。

text.en: The last lesson said routers forward by looking up the destination address in a table. But there are billions of connected devices in the world: if the table had a row for every host, no router could store it, and it could not finish searching.
text.zh: 上一课说到，路由器按目的地址查表转发。可是全球有几十亿台联网设备：如果表里每台主机一行，没有哪台路由器存得下，也查不完。

text.en: The solution is the same as for postal addresses. A letter addressed to “Melbourne · a university · Computer Science department · Level 3, Room 11” needs the international sorting centre to look only at “Melbourne”; only when it arrives locally does anyone look at the university, then the department. IP addresses are layered the same way: **network part + host part**. A distant router looks only at the network part, and all hosts in one network share a single row.
text.zh: 解法和邮政地址一样。一封寄往「墨尔本 · 某大学 · 计算机系 · 3 楼 11 号」的信，国际分拣中心只需要看「墨尔本」，到了本地才看大学，再看系。IP 地址也这样分层：**网络部分 + 主机部分**。远处的路由器只看网络部分，同一个网络里的所有主机共用一行。

text.en: So the router's table remembers “networks”, not “hosts”. Billions of hosts become a far smaller number of networks.
text.zh: 所以路由器的表里记的是「网络」，不是「主机」。几十亿台主机，变成数量小得多的网络。

body.en: The analogy is not perfect: the hierarchy of a postal address is written in words, while the hierarchy of an IP address is hidden in the first half of 32 binary bits. The next page looks at these 32 bits.
body.zh: 类比不完全：邮政地址的层次写在文字里，IP 地址的层次藏在 32 位二进制的前半段里。下一页就看这 32 位。

intro.en: An IPv4 address is 32 bits long. To make it readable, it is cut into groups of 8 bits, each written as a decimal number, with dots in between: **dotted decimal**. The largest value of a group is $2^8-1=255$, so each group runs from 0 to 255. To turn 128.18.3.11 back into 32 bits, the place values in each group from left to right are 128, 64, 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1.
intro.zh: IPv4 地址长 32 位。为了好读，每 8 位一段，写成四个十进制数，中间用点隔开，叫**点分十进制** (dotted decimal)。每段最大是 $2^8-1=255$，所以每段取值 0 到 255。把 128.18.3.11 还原成 32 位，每一段的位权从左到右是 128、64、32、16、8、4、2、1。

why.en: 128 is exactly the place value of the leftmost bit, so only that bit is 1.
why.zh: 128 正好是最左一位的位权，只有那一位是 1。

why.en: 18 = 16 + 2, so the bits with place values 16 and 2 are 1. This is the group drawn in the slides' figure.
why.zh: 18 = 16 + 2，权为 16 和 2 的两位是 1。这就是课件图里画的那一段。

why.en: The four groups put together make exactly 32 bits.
why.zh: 四段拼起来，正好 32 位。

outro.en: 32 bits can write $2^{32}=4\,294\,967\,296$ addresses, about 4.3 billion. The world's connected devices outgrew that long ago, and addresses have run short: the slides only put a question mark on this problem. There are three remedies: hand out addresses more thriftily (this lesson's CIDR), let many devices share one address (NAT), and move to longer addresses (IPv6). The last two are covered in the next lesson. Addresses are managed and allocated centrally by ICANN (Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers).
outro.zh: 32 位一共能写出 $2^{32}=4\,294\,967\,296$ 个地址，约 43 亿。全世界的联网设备早就比这多，地址不够用了：这个问题课件只打了一个问号。办法有三条：更省着分地址（本课的 CIDR）、让很多设备共用一个地址（NAT）、换更长的地址（IPv6）。后两条下一课讲。地址由 ICANN（Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers）统一管理和分配。

title.en: Prefix: a beginning that stands for a whole block
title.zh: 前缀：用一个开头代表一整块

text.en: Addresses are not handed out one by one but in **blocks**: all the hosts in a block share the same network part. For example, the 256-address block 128.18.3.0 to 128.18.3.255 has the same first 24 bits, and the last 8 are free.
text.zh: 地址不是一个个发的，而是**成块** (block) 分配：同一块里的所有主机，共享同一个网络部分。例：256 个地址的块 128.18.3.0 到 128.18.3.255，前 24 位都一样，后 8 位随便。

text.en: Such a block is marked with a **prefix**, written as “lowest address/length in bits”:
text.zh: 这样的块用**前缀** (prefix) 来标记，写成「最低地址/位长」：

items.en: `128.18.3.0/24`: the first 24 bits are fixed and the last $32-24=8$ bits are free, so there are $2^{8}$ = 256 addresses, from 128.18.3.0 to 128.18.3.255.
`18.2.0.0/16`: the first 16 bits are fixed and the last 16 are free, so there are $2^{16}$ = 65,536 addresses, from 18.2.0.0 to 18.2.255.255.

text.en: In general, a block with prefix /L has $2^{32-L}$ addresses. The larger L is, the more bits are fixed and the smaller the block.
text.zh: 一般地，前缀 /L 的块有 $2^{32-L}$ 个地址。L 越大，固定的位越多，块越小。

text.en: There is one more rule: **a block must start at a multiple of its size**, that is, the free bits at the end must be all 0 in the starting address. So 128.18.3.0/24 is legal, and 128.18.3.128/24 is not (the last 8 bits are not all 0); but 128.18.3.128/25 is legal: it is 128 addresses, from .128 to .255.
text.zh: 还有一条规矩：**块的起点必须是块大小的整数倍**，也就是后面那些自由的位，在起点地址里必须全是 0。所以 128.18.3.0/24 合法，128.18.3.128/24 不合法（后 8 位不全是 0）；而 128.18.3.128/25 合法：它是 128 个地址，从 .128 到 .255。

body.en: The first address in a block (host bits all 0) is called the network address, and the last (host bits all 1) is the broadcast address; neither can be assigned to a host. So in a block of 256 addresses, 254 can actually be assigned to hosts.
body.zh: 块里第一个地址（主机位全 0）叫网络地址，最后一个（主机位全 1）是广播地址，都不能分给主机。所以 256 个地址的块，实际能分给主机的是 254 个。

title.en: Work out the range of a block

prompt.en: For the address block with prefix 172.16.48.0/20, write its last address in the form 172.16.x.255. What is x?
prompt.zh: 前缀 172.16.48.0/20 这个地址块，最后一个地址写成 172.16.x.255 的形式，x 是多少？

hints.en: The first two groups of /20 are 16 bits, and in the third group 4 bits are fixed and 4 are free. 48 in binary is 0011 0000.
hints.zh: /20 的前两段共 16 位，第三段固定 4 位、自由 4 位。48 写成二进制是 0011 0000。

explain.en: /20 has 12 host bits: the last 4 bits of the third group plus the whole fourth group. 48 = 0011 0000, and its last 4 bits are all 0, so the start is aligned. With the last 4 bits all 1, the third group is 0011 1111 = 63. So the range is 172.16.48.0 to 172.16.63.255, $2^{12}$ = 4096 addresses in all.

title.en: Subnet mask: picking out the network part
title.zh: 子网掩码：把网络部分挑出来

text.en: Given a destination address, how does a router know which bits are the network part? Using the **subnet mask**: a 32-bit number whose **network part is all 1s and host part all 0s**. For prefix length L, it is L 1s followed by $32-L$ 0s.
text.zh: 路由器拿到一个目的地址，怎么知道网络部分是哪几位？靠**子网掩码** (subnet mask)：一个 32 位的数，**网络部分全是 1，主机部分全是 0**。前缀长 L，就是 L 个 1 再接 $32-L$ 个 0。

text.en: Take the **bitwise AND** of the address and the mask: the result bit is 1 only if both bits are 1. Where the mask has a 1, the bit is left as it is; where it has a 0, the bit always becomes 0. The result is the network part, with the host part cleared.
text.zh: 把地址和掩码做**按位与** (bitwise AND)：两位都是 1，结果才是 1。掩码里是 1 的位，原样留下；是 0 的位，一律变成 0。结果就是网络部分，主机部分被清零。

text.en: Example: 128.18.3.11 AND 255.255.255.0. The first three groups are unchanged when ANDed with 255, and the last group becomes 0 when ANDed with 0, giving 128.18.3.0. Only when the mask is not a whole group do you need to write that group in binary. Another one: 192.24.13.5 AND 255.255.252.0, where only the third group needs working out.
text.zh: 例：128.18.3.11 与 255.255.255.0 按位与。前三段与 255 相与不变，最后一段与 0 相与变成 0，得 128.18.3.0。掩码不是整段时，才需要把那一段写成二进制。再看一个：192.24.13.5 与 255.255.252.0，只有第三段需要算。

text.en: The result is 192.24.12.0: the address 192.24.13.5 belongs to the network 192.24.12.0/22. This example will be used again below.

title.en: Routing table: network, mask, outgoing line

text.en: Each row of a routing table is a triple: **destination network**, **subnet mask**, **outgoing line** (physical or virtual).
text.zh: 路由表的每一行是一个三元组：**目的网络**、**子网掩码**、**出线**（物理的或虚拟的）。

text.en: How does the router use it? For each row: AND the packet's destination address with that row's mask, and see whether the result equals that row's destination network. If equal, it is a match, and the packet is sent out on that row's outgoing line.
text.zh: 路由器怎么用它？对每一行：把包的目的地址和这一行的掩码按位与，看结果是否等于这一行的目的网络。相等，就是匹配，从这一行的出线送出去。

text.en: Example: destination address 128.18.3.77 ANDed with 255.255.255.0 gives 128.18.3.0, equal to the destination network, so it matches and goes out on Eth 0. Destination address 128.18.4.77 ANDed gives 128.18.4.0, which is not equal, so it does not match.
What if several rows match? Keep that question for now; “longest prefix matching” later answers it.
text.zh: 如果好几行都匹配怎么办？先留着这个问题，后面「最长前缀匹配」回答。

text.en: A table often has a row 0.0.0.0/0: the mask is all 0s, and any address ANDed with it gives 0.0.0.0, so it matches everything. It is called the **default route**, and it catches packets that “no other row recognises”, handing them to the next router closer to the outside (whose address is called the next hop). Your laptop works the same way: apart from the local network, everything is handed to the router in the dorm.
text.zh: 表里常有一行 0.0.0.0/0：掩码全是 0，任何地址与它相与都得 0.0.0.0，所以什么都匹配。它叫**默认路由**，专门收「别的行都认不得」的包，交给更靠近外面的下一台路由器（它的地址叫下一跳）。你的笔记本也是这样：除了本地网络，其余的全部交给宿舍的路由器。

chapter.zh: 地址块怎么发才不浪费

prompt.en: The early Internet handed out blocks of only three sizes: about 16.77 million addresses, 65,536, and 256. A school has 2000 machines that need to be online, and each organisation can take only one block. What is the most sensible block for it to take?
prompt.zh: 早期互联网只发三种大小的块：约 1677 万个地址、65,536 个、256 个。一所学校有 2000 台要上网的机器，每个机构只能领一个块。它最合理的领法是？

label.en: Take a block of 256: use it for now and sort it out when it runs short.
label.zh: 领 256 个的块：先用着，不够再说。

feedback.en: 256 cannot even hold the remainder of 2000 machines, so it fails from the start.
feedback.zh: 256 个连 2000 台机器的零头都装不下，一开始就不行。

label.en: Take a block of 65,536: enough, but very wasteful.
label.zh: 领 65,536 个的块：够用，但浪费很大。

label.en: Take the block of about 16.77 million: bigger is less worry.
label.zh: 领约 1677 万个的块：大一点省心。

feedback.en: It would fit, but waste even more; and there are only 128 such big blocks in the whole world, so they could not be handed out like this.
feedback.zh: 装得下，但浪费得更多；而且这种大块全世界一共只有 128 个，不可能这样发。

label.en: Take 8 blocks of 256 and combine them.
label.zh: 领 8 个 256 的块，凑起来用。

feedback.en: The question limits it to one block. And splitting into 8 blocks would add 8 rows to the tables of distant routers, which is just what we want to avoid later.
feedback.zh: 题里限定只能领一个块。而且拆成 8 块，远处路由器的表里就多出 8 行，这正是后面要避免的。

explain.en: There are only three sizes, with nothing in the middle that “just fits”. 2000 machines can only take a block of 65,536, wasting 65,536 − 2000 = 63,536 addresses, about 97%. This problem is the reason CIDR appeared.
explain.zh: 只有三档大小，中间没有「刚好够用」的。2000 台只能领 65,536 的块，浪费 65,536 − 2000 = 63,536 个地址，约 97%。这个问题，就是 CIDR 出现的原因。

title.en: Classful addressing: the block size is written at the start of the address
title.zh: 分类编址：块的大小写在地址开头

text.en: The earliest method is called **classful addressing**: addresses are allocated in blocks of fixed sizes, in five classes, and **the first few bits of an address say which class it is**, that is, how big the block is. A router looks at the beginning and knows how many bits the network part has, with no separate mask needed.
text.zh: 最早的办法叫**分类编址** (classful addressing)：地址按固定大小的块分配，分五类，**用地址开头的几位说明它是哪一类**，也就是块多大。路由器一看开头，就知道网络部分有几位，不需要另外的掩码。

text.en: How many blocks in each class: class A's beginning takes 1 bit, leaving only 7 bits of network part, so only $2^{7}$ = 128 blocks; class B has $2^{14}$ = 16,384 blocks; class C has $2^{21}$ = 2,097,152 blocks. Classes D and E are not used in this lesson.
text.zh: 每类有多少块：A 类开头占去 1 位，网络部分只剩 7 位，只有 $2^{7}$ = 128 块；B 类有 $2^{14}$ = 16,384 块；C 类有 $2^{21}$ = 2,097,152 块。D、E 两类本课不用。

text.en: The problem is that there are only three sizes and nothing in between. An organisation that needs 2000 hosts: class C's 256 is not enough, so it can only take class B's 65,536, wasting 65,536 − 2000 = 63,536, about 97%. The big blocks were also used up very quickly.
text.zh: 问题出在大小只有三档，没有中间的。一个需要 2000 台主机的机构：C 类 256 个不够，只能领 B 类 65,536 个，浪费 65,536 − 2000 = 63,536 个，约 97%。大块还很快就发完了。

text.en: The remedy is to go **classless**: the block size is no longer decided by the class at the start of the address, but by an explicit **prefix length** /L, which can be any power of 2. 2000 hosts need $2^{11}$ = 2048 addresses (and with the network address and broadcast address set aside, 2000 + 2 ≤ 2048), so take a /21, and the waste is only 48. This is **CIDR** (Classless Inter-Domain Routing).
text.zh: 解决的办法是**无类别** (classless)：块的大小不再由地址开头的类来定，而是由一个明写的**前缀长度** /L 来定，可以是任何 2 的幂。2000 台主机，要 $2^{11}$ = 2048 个地址（再留出网络地址和广播地址，2000 + 2 ≤ 2048），领一个 /21，浪费只有 48 个。这就是 **CIDR** (Classless Inter-Domain Routing)。

title.en: Subnetting: one prefix outside, several blocks inside
title.zh: 子网划分：对外一个前缀，对内切成几块

text.en: An ISP gives the University of Melbourne a prefix 128.208.0.0/16, $2^{16}$ = 65,536 addresses in all (this is the slides' example, not the university's real addresses). Inside the university there are three departments, EE, CS and Art, each needing a block. **Subnetting** is cutting one network into several blocks internally while it still looks like one network from outside: outside routers need only one row, 128.208.0.0/16.
text.zh: ISP 给墨尔本大学一个前缀 128.208.0.0/16，共 $2^{16}$ = 65,536 个地址（这是课件的示例，不是学校真实的地址）。学校内部有 EE、CS、Art 三个系，各要一块。**子网划分** (subnetting) 就是把一个网络在内部切成几块，对外仍然像一个网络：外面的路由器只需要一行 128.208.0.0/16。

text.en: How to cut? Look at the third group: after /16, the third group is the high 8 bits of the host part. The slides' way of cutting is **largest first, and aligned on boundaries**.
text.zh: 怎么切？看第三段：/16 之后，第三段是主机部分的高 8 位。课件的切法是**最大的先分，并且按边界对齐**。

alt.en: 128.208.0.0/16 cut into four blocks by the third group: EE takes 0 to 63, Art takes 64 to 95, 96 to 127 is spare, and CS takes 128 to 255
alt.zh: 128.208.0.0/16 按第三段切成四块：EE 占 0 到 63，Art 占 64 到 95，96 到 127 留着，CS 占 128 到 255

caption.en: The whole horizontal axis is all the addresses of the /16; the four blocks fill it exactly, with no overlap.
caption.zh: 整条横轴是 /16 的全部地址，四块拼满，没有重叠。

text.en: How to read it: CS needs the largest block and takes half: its third group begins with 1, fixing just 1 bit, prefix /17. EE takes the first half of the remaining half: it begins with 00, fixing 2 bits, prefix /18. Art takes another small block: it begins with 010, fixing 3 bits, prefix /19. The block beginning with 011 is not handed out and is kept for future use.
text.zh: 读法：CS 要最大的一块，拿下一半：第三段以 1 开头，只固定 1 位，前缀 /17。EE 取剩下一半的前一半：以 00 开头，固定 2 位，前缀 /18。Art 再取一小块：以 010 开头，固定 3 位，前缀 /19。以 011 开头的那块没有分出去，留着将来用。

text.en: Why largest first, and aligned? A block must start at a multiple of its own size. If small blocks were placed first, the large block could not find a suitable starting point and a gap would have to be left.
text.zh: 为什么大的先分、要对齐？一块的起点必须是它自己大小的整数倍。如果先把小块摆在最前面，大块就找不到合适的起点，只好空出一段。

body.en: As long as blocks do not overlap and each block's start is aligned, any layout is legal. The slides' layout has EE first, CS in the second half, and Art in between. Exam questions usually state the order, such as “largest first, each time take the lowest free aligned block”; just follow the order the question gives.
body.zh: 只要块和块不重叠、每块的起点对齐，怎么摆都合法。课件的摆法是 EE 在最前、CS 在后半、Art 夹在中间。考试题通常会把顺序写明，比如「大的先分，每次取最低的空闲对齐块」，按题目写的顺序做就行。

text.en: Outwardly only one 128.208.0.0/16 is exposed. Routers inside the university forward by the first few bits of the third group: those beginning with 1 go to CS, those beginning with 00 go to EE, and those beginning with 010 go to Art.
text.zh: 对外只露一个 128.208.0.0/16。学校内部的路由器则看第三段的开头几位转发：以 1 开头的去 CS，以 00 开头的去 EE，以 010 开头的去 Art。

prompt.en: An organisation has been given 10.5.0.0/16 and must divide it among three departments: X needs 30,000 addresses, Y needs 12,000, and Z needs 3,000. The method is “largest first, each time take the lowest aligned free block”, so X has first received 10.5.0.0/17. Which prefix does Y get?
prompt.zh: 某单位领到 10.5.0.0/16，内部要分给三个部门：X 需要 30,000 个地址，Y 需要 12,000 个，Z 需要 3,000 个。分法是「大的先分，每次取最低的、对齐的空闲块」，所以 X 先拿到了 10.5.0.0/17。Y 得到的前缀是哪个？

feedback.en: A /17 has 32,768 addresses, far more than the 12,000 Y needs; 12,000 needs only $2^{14}$ = 16,384, which is a /18.
X already holds 10.5.0.0/17, that is, third group 0 to 127, which includes 64 to 127. Y's block cannot overlap X's.
feedback.zh: X 已经占了 10.5.0.0/17，也就是第三段 0 到 127，其中包含 64 到 127。Y 的块不能和 X 重叠。

feedback.en: 10.5.12.0 is not a legal start for a /18 block: a /18 block is 16,384 addresses, and the third group can only start at 0, 64, 128 or 192. The start must be a multiple of the block size.
feedback.zh: 10.5.12.0 不是 /18 块的合法起点：/18 的块是 16,384 个地址，第三段只能从 0、64、128、192 开始。起点必须是块大小的整数倍。

explain.en: X needs 30,000, and $2^{15}$ = 32,768 is enough, so it is a /17, taking 10.5.0.0/17 (third group 0 to 127). Y needs 12,000, and $2^{14}$ = 16,384 is enough, so it is a /18; by the rule of taking the lowest aligned free block, the first aligned start after X is third group 128, so Y is 10.5.128.0/18 (128 to 191). Z needs 3,000, and $2^{12}$ = 4,096 is enough, so it is a /20, giving 10.5.192.0/20. If the question did not state the order, putting Y at 10.5.192.0/18 would be equally legal, which is why exam questions state the order.

text.en: Subnetting cuts one block smaller. In the other direction, small blocks also have to be merged into larger ones. A backbone router has to store one row for each of millions of networks worldwide, which eats memory and computing power and makes lookups slow: this is called **routing table explosion**. The remedy is **aggregation**: merge several prefixes into one larger prefix and announce just one row to the outside.
text.zh: 子网划分是把一块切小。反过来，也要把小块合大。骨干路由器要为全球几百万个网络各存一行，吃内存和算力，查表也慢：这叫**路由表爆炸** (routing table explosion)。办法是**聚合** (aggregation)：把几个前缀合成一个更大的前缀，对外只说一行。

text.en: Start with the cleanest case: four adjacent /24s whose third groups are 0, 1, 2 and 3, which in binary are 000000xx. Their first 22 bits are exactly the same, and together they are exactly 10.0.0.0/22: 4 × 256 = 1024 addresses, no more and no fewer. Four rows become one.
text.zh: 先看最干净的一种：四个相邻的 /24，第三段分别是 0、1、2、3，写成二进制是 000000xx。它们的前 22 位完全相同，合起来正好是 10.0.0.0/22：4 × 256 = 1024 个地址，不多不少。四行变成一行。

text.en: To merge like this three conditions must hold: the prefixes are **contiguous**; **aligned**, so that together they are exactly one legal larger block (the start is a multiple of the larger block's size); and together they are **neither more nor fewer**, covering exactly all the addresses of the shorter prefix. A counter-example: 10.0.1.0/24 plus 10.0.2.0/24 cannot merge into a /23, because a /23 block can only start at 10.0.0.0 or 10.0.2.0, and 10.0.1.0 is not a legal start.
text.zh: 能这样合，要满足三个条件：这几个前缀**连续**；**对齐**，合起来恰好是一个合法的大块（起点是大块大小的整数倍）；合起来**不多不少**，正好覆盖那个更短前缀的全部地址。反例：10.0.1.0/24 加 10.0.2.0/24 合不成一个 /23，因为 /23 的块只能从 10.0.0.0 或 10.0.2.0 起，10.0.1.0 不是合法的起点。

text.en: Now the slides' example: below London's router hang three networks.
text.zh: 再看课件的例子：London 的路由器下面接着三个网络。

text.en: From the New York router's far-away point of view, these three networks all lie towards London, and it can write just one row, 192.24.0.0/19 ($2^{13}$ = 8,192 addresses, third group 0 to 31). Three rows become one.
text.zh: 在远处的 New York 路由器看来，这三个网络都往 London 去，可以只写一行 192.24.0.0/19（$2^{13}$ = 8,192 个地址，第三段 0 到 31）。三行变成一行。

title.en: This aggregation comes with a hole
title.zh: 这次的聚合带着一个洞

body.en: The three networks' addresses add up to 2,048 + 1,024 + 4,096 = 7,168, but the aggregated /19 has 8,192, which does not satisfy “neither more nor fewer”. The extra 1,024 are the block with third group 12 to 15: it lies between Edinburgh and Oxford, does not belong to London, and in the slides it belongs to San Francisco (SF). After aggregation, New York would send packets for this block to London as well, wrongly. The remedy is to add one more, longer exception for the hole and let longest prefix matching handle it. The next two pages cover this.
body.zh: 三个网络的地址数加起来是 2,048 + 1,024 + 4,096 = 7,168，聚合出的 /19 却有 8,192 个，不满足「不多不少」。多出来的 1,024 个，是第三段 12 到 15 的那一块：它在 Edinburgh 和 Oxford 之间，不属于 London，课件里它属于 San Francisco（SF）。聚合之后，New York 会把发往这一块的包也送去 London，送错了。办法是为这个洞再加一条更长的例外，靠最长前缀匹配来处理。下面两页讲。

prompt.en: Which of the following groups of prefixes can be aggregated exactly into the shorter prefix written in the option (together neither more nor fewer, covering it exactly)?
prompt.zh: 下面哪一组前缀，可以恰好聚合成选项里写的那个更短的前缀（合起来不多不少，正好覆盖它）？

feedback.en: 10.0.0.0/23 is 10.0.0.0 to 10.0.1.255, containing only 10.0.1.0/24 and not 10.0.2.0/24. The two networks are adjacent, but they are not aligned into the same /23 block.
10.0.0.0/21 is 8 /24s (third group 0 to 7). The ones in between, 1 to 3 and 5 to 7, do not belong to these two networks, and after aggregation other people's packets would be drawn in.
feedback.zh: 10.0.0.0/21 是 8 个 /24（第三段 0 到 7）。中间 1 到 3、5 到 7 都不属于这两个网络，聚合后会把别人的包也吸过来。

feedback.en: Together they have only 2,048 + 4,096 = 6,144 addresses, while a /19 has 8,192. The missing third group 8 to 15 belongs to neither network.
feedback.zh: 它们加起来只有 2,048 + 4,096 = 6,144 个地址，而 /19 有 8,192 个。缺的第三段 8 到 15，不属于这两个网络。

explain.en: 4 adjacent /24s (third group 0, 1, 2, 3) exactly make up 10.0.0.0/22 (third group 0 to 3): contiguous, aligned, and completely covered, so all three conditions are satisfied. In the other groups, either the blocks are not aligned or there is a gap in the middle, and aggregation would draw in addresses that are not its own.
explain.zh: 4 个相邻的 /24（第三段 0、1、2、3）正好拼成 10.0.0.0/22（第三段 0 到 3），连续、对齐、被完整覆盖，三个条件都满足。其余几组要么没对齐，要么中间有缺口，聚合会吸来不属于自己的地址。

title.zh: 最长前缀匹配：例外优先

text.en: After aggregation, an address may match two rows at once: one is the large block (/19), and the other is an exception carved out of the large block (/22). The rule: **among the matching rows, take the one with the longest prefix**, that is, the one whose address block is smallest (longest matching prefix).
text.zh: 聚合之后，一个地址可能同时匹配两行：一行是大块（/19），一行是大块里挖出的例外（/22）。规则：**取匹配的行里前缀最长的**，也就是地址块最小的那一行（最长匹配前缀，longest matching prefix）。

text.en: Why the longest? Because a short prefix is the “general rule” and a long prefix is the “exception”. Exceptions must come first, or they would never take effect, and SF's packets would always be snatched by the /19. It is like a teacher saying: “The whole class go to the playground, but Xiao Ming goes to the infirmary.” Xiao Ming fits both sentences, and listens to the more specific one.
text.zh: 为什么取最长？因为短前缀是「一般规则」，长前缀是「例外」。例外要优先，否则例外永远不会生效，SF 的包会一直被 /19 抢走。像老师说：「全班去操场，但小明去医务室。」小明同时符合两句话，听更具体的那句。

text.en: The New York router's table has only two rows:
text.zh: New York 路由器的表，只有两行：

alt.en: The third group 0 to 31 is divided into four blocks: Cambridge 0 to 7, Edinburgh 8 to 11, SF 12 to 15, Oxford 16 to 31; the SF block is marked orange
alt.zh: 第三段 0 到 31 被分成四块：Cambridge 0 到 7，Edinburgh 8 到 11，SF 12 到 15，Oxford 16 到 31；SF 一块用橙色标出

caption.en: The whole horizontal axis is 192.24.0.0/19. SF sits between London's three networks.
caption.zh: 整条横轴是 192.24.0.0/19。SF 夹在 London 的三个网络之间。

text.en: **Example 1**: a packet is sent to 192.24.13.5. The third group 13 = 0000 1101. Row 1: AND with 252 (1111 1100) gives 0000 1100 = 12, so 192.24.12.0, equal to this row's destination network: a match. Row 2: AND with 224 (1110 0000) gives 0, so 192.24.0.0: also a match. Both rows match, so take the longer /22, and send it from Eth 0 to SF.

**Example 2**: a packet is sent to 192.24.2.7. The third group 2 = 0000 0010. Row 1: AND with 252 gives 0, so 192.24.0.0, which is not equal to 192.24.12.0: no match. Row 2: AND with 224 gives 0: a match. Only one row matches, so it is sent from Eth 1 to London.
text.zh: **例 2**：包发往 192.24.2.7。第三段 2 = 0000 0010。第一行：与 252 相与得 0，得 192.24.0.0，不等于 192.24.12.0，不匹配。第二行：与 224 相与得 0，匹配。只有一行匹配，从 Eth 1 送往 London。

text.en: Forwarding thus becomes more complicated, but more flexible: aggregations and exceptions can be layered on top of each other.
text.zh: 转发因此变复杂了，但更灵活：聚合和例外可以层层叠加。

summary.en: How routers find the longest match quickly (beyond the slides)
summary.zh: 路由器怎么快速找到最长匹配（超出课件）

text.en: Real routers do not compare row by row: they use special data structures (such as a prefix tree) or dedicated hardware (TCAM) to find the longest match in one lookup. The slides only require you to be able to make this choice.
text.zh: 真实的路由器不是一行行去比：它用专门的数据结构（比如前缀树）或专用硬件（TCAM），一次就查出最长匹配。课件只要求你会做这个选择。

intro.en: Why does SF's /22 land exactly inside London's /19, and the four blocks fill it exactly? Write the third group in binary and look only at the fixed leading bits.
intro.zh: 为什么 SF 的 /22 刚好落在 London 的 /19 之内，四块又刚好拼满？把第三段写成二进制，只看固定的开头几位。

why.en: A /19 fixes only the first 3 bits of the third group (000); the other 5 bits plus the 8 bits of the fourth group are free, 13 bits in all.
why.zh: /19 在第三段只固定前 3 位（000），其余 5 位加第四段的 8 位自由，共 13 位。

why.en: A /21 fixes the first 5 bits, and there are $32-21=11$ free bits.
A /22 fixes the first 6 bits: 000010, with 10 free bits.
Also a /22, with first 6 bits 000011, right next to Edinburgh. It too begins with 000, so it is inside London's /19: a block carved out as an exception.
why.zh: 同样是 /22，前 6 位是 000011，紧挨着 Edinburgh。它也以 000 开头，所以在 London 的 /19 之内：是挖出来的一块例外。

why.en: A /20 fixes the first 4 bits: 0001, with 12 free bits.
The four blocks exactly fill the /19, with no overlap and no gap. London's own three blocks add up to 7168, and what the aggregated /19 contains beyond that is SF's 1024.
why.zh: 四块恰好拼满 /19，不重叠也没有缺口。London 自己的三块加起来 7168，聚合后的 /19 多包含的，就是 SF 的 1024。

outro.en: So SF needs its own /22 row in New York's table: this row's prefix is longer than the /19, longest prefix matching makes it take priority, and packets for SF are no longer snatched by London.
outro.zh: 所以 SF 要在 New York 的表里单列一行 /22：这行的前缀比 /19 长，最长前缀匹配会让它优先，发往 SF 的包就不会再被 London 抢走。

title.en: Choose the exit, writing out each bitwise AND
title.zh: 选出口，写出每一步按位与

prompt.en: A router's table has three rows: 10.8.64.0/18 → Eth 1; 10.8.76.0/22 → Eth 2; 0.0.0.0/0 → Eth 0. A packet is sent to 10.8.77.200. Which exit does it go out of? Write out the result of the bitwise AND for each row (third group only), and explain why you choose that row.
prompt.zh: 一台路由器的表有三行：10.8.64.0/18 → Eth 1；10.8.76.0/22 → Eth 2；0.0.0.0/0 → Eth 0。一个包发往 10.8.77.200。它会从哪个出口出去？请写出每一行的按位与（只写第三段）的结果，并说明为什么选这一行。

key_points.en: /18 row: third group 77 = 0100 1101, AND with 192 (1100 0000) gives 64, the network is 10.8.64.0, equal to this row's destination network: a match
/22 row: AND with 252 (1111 1100) gives 76 (0100 1100), the network is 10.8.76.0: a match
Default row 0.0.0.0/0: the mask is all 0s, AND gives 0.0.0.0: also a match
All three rows match, so take the longest prefix, /22, and go out of Eth 2
key_points.zh: 三行都匹配，取前缀最长的 /22，从 Eth 2 出去

model_answer.en: The third group 77 = 0100 1101. /18 row: AND with 192 (1100 0000) gives 0100 0000 = 64, so 10.8.64.0: a match. /22 row: AND with 252 (1111 1100) gives 0100 1100 = 76, so 10.8.76.0: a match. Default row /0: the mask is all 0s, and any address matches. All three rows match, so take the longest prefix, /22, and go out of Eth 2.

hints.en: First write the third group 77 in binary, then AND it with the third group of each of the three masks.
hints.zh: 先把第三段 77 写成二进制，再分别与三个掩码的第三段相与。

explain.en: All three rows match: the /18 covers third group 64 to 127, the /22 covers 76 to 79, and the default row covers everything. 77 falls within all three ranges. Longest prefix matching takes the most specific one, the /22, exit Eth 2. If it took only the first matching row, the packet would be wrongly sent to Eth 1: that is the case of an exception being snatched by the general rule.
explain.zh: 三行都匹配：/18 管第三段 64 到 127，/22 管 76 到 79，默认行管所有。77 同时落在这三个范围里。最长前缀匹配取最具体的那条，也就是 /22，出口 Eth 2。如果只取第一个匹配的行，就会错送到 Eth 1：那是例外被一般规则抢走的情形。

title.en: The IPv4 datagram: 32 bits a row, five rows, 20 bytes
title.zh: IPv4 数据报：一行 32 位，五行 20 字节

text.en: So far we have talked about addresses. Addresses live in the header of an IP datagram. An IPv4 datagram consists of a **header** and a **payload**. The header has a fixed part of 20 bytes, which may be followed by variable-length options.
text.zh: 前面一直在说地址。地址就长在 IP 数据报的头里。IPv4 数据报由**头部** (header) 和**载荷** (payload) 组成。头部有 20 字节的固定部分，后面可以跟长度可变的选项 (options)。

alt.en: IPv4 header: row 1 version, IHL, differentiated services, total length; row 2 identification, DF, MF, fragment offset; row 3 TTL, protocol, header checksum; row 4 source address; row 5 destination address; then options
alt.zh: IPv4 头部：第一行版本、IHL、区分服务、总长度；第二行标识、DF、MF、片偏移；第三行 TTL、协议、头部校验和；第四行源地址；第五行目的地址；最后是选项

caption.en: Colours match the four groups of fields below; grey marks a few self-describing fields.
caption.zh: 颜色对应下面的四组字段；灰色是自我描述的几个字段。

text.en: Reading the figure: each row is 32 bits (4 bytes), and the fixed part is exactly five rows, $5\times4=20$ bytes. The **header length IHL** (Internet Header Length) is in units of 32 bits (4 bytes): the minimum is 5, which is 20 bytes; with options it is larger, and the maximum is 15, which is 60 bytes.
text.zh: 读图：每一行 32 位（4 字节），固定部分正好五行，$5\times4=20$ 字节。**头部长度 IHL** (Internet Header Length) 以 32 位（4 字节）为单位：最小是 5，就是 20 字节；有选项时更大，最大是 15，就是 60 字节。

text.en: You don't need to memorise a dozen-odd fields one by one; split them into four groups:
text.zh: 十来个字段不必一个个死记，分成四组：

items.en: **Who sends to whom**: source address and destination address, 32 bits each.
items.zh: **谁发给谁**：源地址、目的地址，各 32 位。

items.en: **How to fragment**: identification, DF, MF, fragment offset (the third page on).
items.zh: **怎么分片**：标识、DF、MF、片偏移（后面第三页）。

items.en: **How long it lives, and whether it is broken**: time to live (TTL) and header checksum (next page).
items.zh: **能活多久、有没有坏**：生存时间 TTL、头部校验和（下一页）。

items.en: **Who to hand to**: the protocol field, saying whether the payload is TCP or UDP (next page).
items.zh: **交给谁**：协议字段，说明载荷是 TCP 还是 UDP（下一页）。

text.en: The rest: **Version**, 4 bits, which for IPv4 is 4. **Differentiated Services** says which class of service this packet belongs to; for example video-call packets can be marked as priority and background downloads as allowed to be slow. **Total Length**, 16 bits, how many bytes the header plus payload come to, at most $2^{16}-1=65{,}535$ bytes.
text.zh: 剩下几个：**版本** (Version)，4 位，IPv4 就是 4。**区分服务** (Differentiated Services)，说明这个包属于哪一级服务，例如视频通话的包可以标成优先，后台下载的标成可以慢。**总长度** (Total Length)，16 位，头部加载荷一共多少字节，最大是 $2^{16}-1=65{,}535$ 字节。

items.en: Security: states the packet's secrecy level.
items.zh: 安全 (security)：说明这个包的保密等级。

items.en: Strict source routing: the sender writes out the complete path, and every hop must follow it.
items.zh: 严格源路由 (strict source routing)：发送方写出完整路径，每一跳都必须照走。

items.en: Loose source routing: the sender lists only a few routers that must be passed through, and chooses the route in between itself.
items.zh: 宽松源路由 (loose source routing)：发送方只列出必须经过的几个路由器，中间的路自己选。

items.en: Record route: makes every router along the way fill in its own address.
items.zh: 记录路由 (record route)：让沿途的每个路由器把自己的地址填进去。

items.en: Timestamp: makes every router along the way fill in the time it handled the packet.
items.zh: 时间戳 (timestamp)：让沿途的每个路由器填上经手的时间。

text.en: Options make the header length variable, which is exactly why IHL is needed: options take at most 40 bytes, so the header is at most 60 bytes. These options are rarely used; the slides only require knowing that these kinds exist.
text.zh: 选项让头部长度可变，这正是需要 IHL 的原因：选项最多 40 字节，头部最长 60 字节。这些选项很少用到，课件只要求知道有这几种。

text.en: TTL: stopping packets circling a loop forever
text.zh: TTL：防止包在环路里永远转

text.en: **Time to Live** (TTL): the sender gives an initial value (commonly 64 or 128), and each router reduces it by 1; when it reaches 0, the router drops the packet. It is called “time”, but what it actually counts is **hops**.
text.zh: **生存时间** (TTL, Time to Live)：发送方给一个初值（常见 64 或 128），每过一个路由器减 1，减到 0，路由器就把包丢掉。名字叫「时间」，实际数的是**跳数**。

text.en: Why is it needed? Routing tables occasionally go wrong, and several routers may point at each other: A hands to B, B hands back to A, and the packet goes round and round the loop. Without TTL, this packet would circle forever, piling up and clogging the lines. With TTL, it is dropped after a few dozen laps, and the network is not dragged to death.
text.zh: 为什么要它？路由表偶尔会出错，几台路由器可能互相指着对方：A 交给 B，B 又交回 A，包在环里一圈圈地转。没有 TTL，这个包会永远转下去，越积越多，把线路塞满。有了 TTL，转几十圈就被丢掉，网络不会被拖死。

text.en: The traceroute tool deliberately sets TTL to 1, 2, 3, ..., so that the routers along the way report themselves in turn when the TTL runs out, which draws out a route.
text.zh: traceroute 工具故意把 TTL 设成 1、2、3……，让沿途的路由器依次因为 TTL 耗尽而回报自己，就画出了一条路。

text.en: Protocol: who to hand to
text.zh: 协议：交给谁

text.en: When a packet reaches the destination host, which transport-layer protocol should the IP layer hand the payload to? Look at the **Protocol** field: 6 means TCP and 17 means UDP. It is like the department written on an envelope. This is the entrance to lessons 11 and 12 (TCP and UDP).
text.zh: 包到了目的主机，IP 层要把载荷交给传输层的哪一个协议？看**协议** (Protocol) 字段：6 表示 TCP，17 表示 UDP。就像信封上写着收件的部门。这是第 11、12 课（TCP 与 UDP）的入口。

text.en: Header checksum: only the header, recomputed at every hop
text.zh: 头部校验和：只管头，每跳重算

text.en: The **Header Checksum** checks only whether the **header** has an error, not the payload. Why? The payload is checked by the transport layer (TCP, UDP) itself; and since a router has to compute it at every hop, computing just the 20-byte header is much faster than computing the whole packet.
text.zh: **头部校验和** (Header Checksum) 只检查**头部**有没有出错，不管载荷。为什么？载荷由传输层（TCP、UDP）自己校验；而路由器每一跳都要算，只算 20 字节的头，比算整个包快得多。

text.en: Moreover, it must be **recomputed at every router**: TTL changes at every hop, so the header changes and the checksum must change with it. The router's actions are: check the checksum and drop the packet if it is wrong; reduce TTL by 1; recompute the checksum; then forward.
text.zh: 而且**每过一个路由器都要重算**：TTL 每一跳都变了，头部变了，校验和就得跟着变。路由器的动作是：检查校验和，不对就丢；TTL 减 1；重新算校验和；再转发。

title.en: Three checks, each covering one stretch

body.en: The IP header checksum protects the header; the link layer's CRC protects the whole frame, over one link only; the transport layer's checksum protects the payload, between the two ends.
body.zh: IP 头部校验和保护头部；链路层的 CRC 保护整个帧，只管一段链路；传输层的校验和保护载荷，管两端之间。

prompt.en: When a router forwards an IPv4 packet, why must it recompute the header checksum?
prompt.zh: 路由器转发一个 IPv4 包时，为什么必须重新计算头部校验和？

label.en: Because the payload is rewritten at every hop.
label.zh: 因为载荷每经过一跳都会被改写。

feedback.en: Routers do not change the payload. What changes at every hop is the TTL in the header.
feedback.zh: 路由器不改载荷。每一跳变的是头部里的 TTL。

label.en: Because TTL is reduced by 1 at every hop, the header has changed, and the old checksum is no longer right.
label.zh: 因为 TTL 每过一跳减 1，头部变了，旧的校验和就不对了。

label.en: Because there is a new link-layer frame, and the checksum must agree with the CRC.
label.zh: 因为换了新的链路层帧，校验和要和 CRC 保持一致。

feedback.en: The IP header checksum and the link layer's CRC are two separate things and do not depend on each other.
feedback.zh: IP 头部校验和和链路层的 CRC 是两回事，互不依赖。

label.en: Because the router uses it to verify whether the payload has an error.
label.zh: 因为路由器要用它验证载荷有没有出错。

feedback.en: The header checksum covers only the header. The payload is protected by the transport layer's own checksum.
feedback.zh: 头部校验和只覆盖头部。载荷由传输层自己的校验和保护。

explain.en: The header checksum is a function of all the header's fields. TTL is reduced by 1 at every hop, so the header changes and the checksum must be recomputed with it, or the next hop would think the header was damaged and drop the packet. The payload has not changed and is not within the checksum's scope.
explain.zh: 头部校验和是头部所有字段的函数。TTL 每过一跳减 1，头部变了，校验和必须跟着重算，否则下一跳会以为头部坏了而丢包。载荷没有变，也不在校验范围内。

title.en: Fragmentation fields: matching them with the last lesson
title.zh: 分片字段：和上一课对上号

text.en: The last lesson taught fragmentation in a simplified form: packet number, byte offset, end bit. In the real IPv4 header, the corresponding fields are:
text.zh: 上一课用简化版讲分片：包号、字节偏移、结束位。真实的 IPv4 头里，对应的字段是：

rows.en: All fragments of one datagram share the same identification; the destination host uses it to sort them into piles
rows.zh: 同一个数据报的所有片，标识都相同；目的主机靠它分堆
片偏移 Fragment offset（13 位）

rows.en: The unit is 8 bytes, not 1 byte
rows.zh: 单位是 8 字节，不是 1 字节

rows.en: Exactly the opposite: MF = 1 means more follow, and the last fragment has MF = 0
rows.zh: 正相反：MF = 1 表示后面还有，最后一片 MF = 0

rows.en: DF = 1: fragmentation not allowed, used for path MTU discovery
rows.zh: DF = 1：不许分片，用于路径 MTU 发现

title.en: MF is the opposite of the end bit

body.en: MF = 1 means “more follow”, while end bit = 1 means “this is the last one”. The slides describe MF as “whether this is the last fragment”, which is easy to read backwards: only MF = 0 is the last fragment.
body.zh: MF = 1 是「后面还有」，结束位 = 1 是「这是最后一个」。课件把 MF 描述成「是不是最后一片」，很容易读反：MF = 0 才是最后一片。

text.en: Why is the offset in units of 8 bytes? The fragment offset has only 13 bits, while the total length can be up to 65,535 bytes. 13 bits can count at most $2^{13}=8192$ units, and at 8 bytes a unit that covers exactly $8192\times8=65{,}536$ bytes. The price is that, except for the last fragment, the data length of every fragment must be a multiple of 8.
text.zh: 为什么偏移以 8 字节为单位？片偏移只有 13 位，而总长度最大 65,535 字节。13 位最多数到 $2^{13}=8192$ 个单位，每单位 8 字节，正好覆盖 $8192\times8=65{,}536$ 字节。代价是：除了最后一片，每一片的数据长度必须是 8 的倍数。

text.en: Example: a datagram with a total length of 4000 bytes (20-byte header, 3980-byte payload) has to cross a network with an MTU of 1500. Each fragment can carry at most $1500-20=1480$ bytes of data, and 1480 is exactly a multiple of 8:
text.zh: 例：一个总长度 4000 字节的数据报（头 20 字节，载荷 3980 字节），要过 MTU 为 1500 的网络。每片最多装 $1500-20=1480$ 字节的数据，1480 正好是 8 的倍数：

text.en: The data of the three fragments: 1480 + 1480 + 1020 = 3980, not a byte out. Every fragment has its own 20-byte header, so after fragmentation 2 extra headers are sent, 40 bytes in all. The destination host sorts them into piles by identification and arranges them by offset; only when it sees MF = 0 and no hole in the middle is reassembly complete.
text.zh: 三片的数据：1480 + 1480 + 1020 = 3980，一个字节不差。每一片都有自己的 20 字节头，所以分片之后多传了 2 个头，共 40 字节。目的主机按标识分堆，按偏移排好，看到 MF = 0 并且中间没有空洞，才算重组完成。

prompt.en: A datagram has a total length of 2820 bytes (20-byte header, 2800-byte payload) and has to cross a network with an MTU of 1000, each fragment having a 20-byte header. What is the value of the “fragment offset” field of fragment 2?
prompt.zh: 一个数据报总长度 2820 字节（头 20 字节，载荷 2800 字节），要经过 MTU 为 1000 的网络，每片的头都是 20 字节。第 2 片的「片偏移」字段值是多少？

hints.en: Each fragment carries at most 980 bytes of data, but except for the last fragment the data length must be a multiple of 8.
hints.zh: 每片最多装 980 字节数据，但除了最后一片，数据长度必须是 8 的倍数。

explain.en: The data is at most $1000-20=980$ bytes; 980 is not a multiple of 8, so take the largest multiple not exceeding it, 976 (= 8 × 122). Fragment 1 has 976 bytes of data and offset 0. Fragment 2 starts from byte 976, so offset = 976 ÷ 8 = 122, and it also carries 976 bytes. Fragment 3 has offset 1952 ÷ 8 = 244 and carries the remaining 848 bytes, with MF = 0.
explain.zh: 数据最多 $1000-20=980$ 字节；980 不是 8 的倍数，取不超过它的最大倍数 976（= 8 × 122）。第 1 片数据 976 字节，偏移 0。第 2 片从第 976 个字节开始，偏移 = 976 ÷ 8 = 122，也装 976 字节。第 3 片偏移 1952 ÷ 8 = 244，装剩下的 848 字节，MF = 0。

text.en: The packet your laptop sends to the school website has in its header everything met in this lesson:
text.zh: 你的笔记本发往学校网站的包，头里有这一课碰到的每一样东西：

rows.en: ANDed with the mask of each row to find the matching rows, taking the one with the longest prefix, to decide the outgoing line
rows.zh: 与每一行的掩码按位与，找出匹配的行，取前缀最长的，决定出线

rows.en: Reduced by 1 at every hop, dropped on reaching 0, to avoid circling a loop forever
rows.zh: 每过一跳减 1，到 0 就丢，避免在环里永远转

rows.en: Checked at every hop, and recomputed because the TTL changed
rows.zh: 每一跳检查，并因为 TTL 变了而重算

rows.en: When a network with a smaller MTU is met, decide whether it can be fragmented, how, and how to reassemble
rows.zh: 遇到 MTU 更小的网络时，决定能不能分片、怎么分、怎么重组

rows.en: On reaching the destination host, decides whether to hand the payload to TCP or UDP
rows.zh: 到了目的主机，决定把载荷交给 TCP 还是 UDP

text.en: Routers rely on the hierarchy of addresses to squeeze billions of hosts into a few rows: one network shares one prefix, several prefixes aggregate into a shorter prefix, and exceptions are caught by longest prefix matching.
text.zh: 路由器靠地址的层次，把几十亿台主机压成几行：同一个网络共用一个前缀，几个前缀再聚合成更短的前缀，例外用最长前缀匹配兜住。

text.en: Two questions remain unanswered: what to do when 32-bit addresses run short (NAT and IPv6), and who fills in the “outgoing line” in the routing table (routing algorithms). The next lesson (lesson 10) takes them up.
text.zh: 还有两个问题没答：32 位地址不够用怎么办（NAT 和 IPv6），路由表里的「出线」又是谁填的（路由算法）。下一课（第 10 课）接着讲。
